rationale: The older Next items as the user decided: serde for Graph and Tree done (no_std too); Alfred onto crypt asked of Alfred (graft 01a15b9e); persisted snapshots and a reverse-relation index dropped with the measurements behind it. The structures' no-std rule now says serde comes with its own feature.

ops.reason: Not needed at today's sizes: the longest Tend history is tend's own (187 batches, 0.6 MB; vg-paradigms 67, alfred 52, sylva 31, parda 25), and tend's hub replays a project's history on load quickly. Revisit if a history grows into tens of thousands of batches.

Graphs already answer 'what points at this' in O(degree) (in_edges, Dir::In), and the one application keeping a reverse index of its own is Alfred (links.rs backlinks): one user isn't a pattern. Extract it when a second project builds the same.
sylva's half is done (crypt shipped in 0.1.0, byte-compatible); the rest is Alfred's change, asked of it in graft 01a15b9e.

ops.text: The structures build without std (only alloc) and pull in no uuid or serde_json: std and uuid come with the log and the knowledge model, and serde (with alloc only) with the serde feature.
Graph and Tree serialize their content, and read back checked
ops.why: With the serde feature, a Graph writes {nodes: [{key, data}], edges: [{key, from, to, data}]} in key order and a Tree {nodes: [{key, parent, data}]} in preorder (parents first, siblings in order): content only, so equal structures write the same bytes whatever their slots (tests/serde.rs checks it after churn). Reading goes through add_node, add_edge and insert, so a duplicate key, a missing parent or an edge to a missing node fails instead of building a broken structure. Sequences rather than maps, so any key type works in any format. The serde feature no longer turns std on: serde is built with alloc, and std adds serde/std, so a no_std user (parda on wasm) can serialize too; CI builds that for wasm32. The round-trip tests use serde_json, so they live in tests/serde.rs, owned by the crate's root rather than Structures, whose rules keep serde_json out of the structures.
